items.question: Why is kāmakalā meditation declared very secret for the best practitioners?
premises: The meditation is called very secret.
It is addressed to best practitioners.
items.inference: The verse presents kāmakalā meditation as esoteric practice reserved for accomplished sādhakas.
uncertainties: Exact ritual referent of kāmakalā is not specified here.
items.plain_english: Thus the very secret meditation on kāmakalā is for the best practitioners.

items.question: What golden radiance is visualized at the genital support in śiva form?

items.plain_english: At the genital place, in the śiva-form support, there is golden radiance.

items.question: What fire-flame and sun radiance are visualized in and above the heart?

items.plain_english: In the heart is fire-flame form; above that is sun radiance.

items.question: What moon-disk and gem-like radiance are visualized at palate and between brows?

items.inference: The verse assigns distinct luminous forms to palate and brow center.

items.plain_english: At the palate is moon-disk likeness; between the brows is gem-like radiance.

items.plain_english: Having held, touched or seen, and meditated upon the kāmakalā body.

items.inference: The verse says an accumulation of emotion arises instantly through reflection.
uncertainties: Whether bhāva means emotion or state is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: In a moment, through such reflection, an accumulation of emotion arises.

items.question: Where does the goddess stand directly as the principle in truth?
premises: The goddess stands in the family.

uncertainties: Kula may mean family, power, or body by context.
items.plain_english: In the family, the goddess stands directly from that principle, in truth.

items.plain_english: The primordial family goddess, immovable, exists for whom she exists.

items.question: What is said to have been told as giving all accomplishments?
items.inference: The verse concludes that kāmakalā meditation has been taught as all-accomplishment-giving.

items.plain_english: Thus the meditation on kāmakalā has been told as giving all accomplishments.

items.question: How should welcome be performed when someone arrives in this ritual context?

uncertainties: The exact ritual action of play-yoga is not defined.
items.plain_english: On arrival, one should give welcome by play-yoga and by one's own play.

items.plain_english: In one's own family, there may be family abundance by fortune-yoga.

items.inference: The verse extends the context to hero-offspring and hero-wife families.

items.plain_english: Thus, having abandoned the family, one should accomplish accomplishment for oneself.

items.plain_english: And the hero-wife is supreme; herself indeed is the great goddess.
